summary: Meta reiterated full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance of roughly 115 billion dollars, with the bulk earmarked for AI data centres and supporting infrastructure. The guide extends the multi-gigawatt campus buildout pattern set by Hyperion and Prometheus.

OpenAI expanded its multi-year compute capacity agreement with CoreWeave, adding roughly 12 billion dollars of contracted GPU capacity through 2030. The deal deepens the neocloud layer's role as overflow capacity for frontier labs.

The Space Development Agency awarded Rocket Lab a contract worth approximately 515 million dollars to design and build satellites for a proliferated low-earth-orbit defence constellation tranche. The award continues the pattern of national-security work flowing to newer launch-and-satellite primes.

GE Vernova committed roughly 600 million dollars to expand US manufacturing of transformers, switchgear, and grid equipment, citing multi-year order backlogs driven by data-centre interconnection queues. Lead times for large power transformers remain measured in years.

TSMC reaffirmed its expanded US investment program of approximately 165 billion dollars covering additional Arizona fabs, advanced packaging facilities, and an R&D centre. The program concentrates leading-edge capacity additions where AI accelerator demand is strongest.

The Department of Defense advanced its microreactor pilot program with Oklo for a powerhouse installation at a remote air base, continuing the federal pattern of acting as first customer for advanced fission. Licensing and fuel availability remain the gating items.

NASA awarded Redwire a contract of approximately 45 million dollars for in-space manufacturing and servicing technology demonstrations. The award adds to a string of small agency contracts that keep early in-space services companies funded ahead of commercial demand.

The Department of Energy awarded Energy Fuels roughly 80 million dollars to expand rare earth separation capacity at its White Mesa mill, part of the federal push to build non-Chinese midstream processing. Domestic separation capacity remains the chain's tightest link.

Vertiv agreed to acquire a privately held liquid-cooling and coolant-distribution specialist for roughly 600 million dollars, deepening its direct-to-chip thermal portfolio. Consolidation in cooling continues as rack densities climb past air-cooling limits.

Microsoft and Constellation Energy progressed their 20-year power purchase agreement covering 835 MW of nuclear output tied to the Crane Clean Energy Center restart, with deliveries ramping toward 2028. Hyperscaler PPAs for firm clean power remain the template other utilities are chasing.

The Department of Defense expanded its offtake and price-floor arrangement with MP Materials covering rare earth magnet output, committing roughly 400 million dollars across the agreement. The deal extends the public-private template for de-risking domestic magnet supply.

The Department of Energy extended its HALEU enrichment contract with Centrus Energy by roughly 110 million dollars, keeping the Piketon cascade producing fuel for advanced reactor demonstrations. Centrus remains the only licensed US HALEU producer.

The US Army placed a production order of approximately 25 million dollars with Red Cat Holdings under its short-range reconnaissance drone program. Small-drone procurement continues to shift toward US-made platforms from emerging vendors.

Amazon guided 2026 capital expenditure to roughly 125 billion dollars, dominated by AWS data-centre, custom-silicon, and power infrastructure spend. Management framed AI capacity as supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained.

US carriers expanded strategic investments and prepayments in AST SpaceMobile by roughly 350 million dollars to accelerate the direct-to-device satellite constellation buildout. Carrier capital continues to substitute for dilutive equity raises in the space segment.

Apple agreed to expand its satellite services arrangement with Globalstar, committing up to 1.1 billion dollars in infrastructure prepayments plus a 400 million dollar equity investment for an approximately 20 percent stake. The funding underwrites a new Globalstar constellation dedicated largely to Apple's iPhone satellite features, substituting customer capital for dilutive raises.

The Space Development Agency awarded L3Harris a contract worth approximately 919 million dollars to build missile-tracking satellites for Tranche 2 of the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture. The award extended the pattern of proliferated-constellation defence spending flowing to satellite primes in batch-sized lots.

SKY Perfect JSAT signed a multi-year agreement worth approximately 230 million dollars with Planet Labs for dedicated high-resolution Pelican satellite capacity, the largest deal in Planet's history at signing. The agreement showed commercial partners funding EO constellation capacity in advance rather than buying imagery spot.

Talen Energy and Amazon expanded their nuclear power agreement, with Talen to supply up to roughly 1,920 MW from the Susquehanna plant through 2042 under a front-of-meter structure. The deal restructured the original behind-the-meter colocation arrangement after FERC pushback, setting the template for hyperscaler-utility contracting in PJM.

Eos Energy closed a Department of Energy Loan Programs Office guaranteed loan of roughly 300 million dollars to expand zinc-based battery manufacturing at its Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania facility. The financing backs a domestically supplied long-duration storage chain outside lithium-ion.

Hitachi Energy announced an additional investment of roughly 1.5 billion dollars to expand global transformer manufacturing capacity through 2027, on top of earlier commitments, citing sustained order growth from grid operators and data centres. Large power transformer lead times remain measured in years despite the buildout.

The US Department of Energy announced roughly 2 billion dollars for 38 projects under the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) program, funding transmission upgrades, grid hardening and smart-grid deployments across dozens of states. The money flows through utilities to equipment makers and specialty contractors.

Meta signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Constellation for the output of the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois beginning in 2027, supporting a roughly 1,121 megawatt plant whose state support was set to expire. The deal extended the hyperscaler-nuclear PPA pattern from restarts to at-risk operating plants.

Amazon and Talen Energy announced an expanded long-term power purchase agreement covering up to 1,920 megawatts of output from the Susquehanna nuclear plant through 2042, restructured as a front-of-the-meter arrangement after regulators questioned the original co-located design. It converted the 2024 Cumulus campus sale into one of the largest corporate nuclear supply deals on record.

The Department of Energy awarded HALEU enrichment contracts to four companies, including Centrus Energy and Urenco USA, under a program with a disclosed ceiling of roughly 2.7 billion dollars. The awards seed a domestic HALEU supply chain for advanced reactors that until then rested on a single Centrus demonstration cascade in Ohio.

NexGen announced its first uranium sales agreements, covering about 5 million pounds of future Rook I production for delivery to multiple US utilities between 2029 and 2033 at market-related pricing. The contracts marked the first utility validation of the still-unbuilt Arrow deposit and of the broader developer tier.

SK hynix announced an investment of approximately 3.87 billion dollars to build an advanced packaging fabrication and R&D facility for HBM in West Lafayette, Indiana, its first US packaging plant. The project, developed alongside Purdue University, brings high-bandwidth memory packaging for AI accelerators onshore.

The US Commerce Department finalized up to 1.61 billion dollars in CHIPS Act direct funding for Texas Instruments, supporting new 300mm fabs in Sherman, Texas and Lehi, Utah. The award backs more than 18 billion dollars of planned analog and embedded processing capacity, with spending flowing to equipment and subsystem suppliers through the decade.

NVIDIA named Navitas Semiconductor among the collaborators on its 800-volt HVDC data-centre power architecture planned for next-generation AI racks. No financial terms were disclosed, but the announcement repriced the wide-bandgap power semiconductor niche around AI data-centre power delivery.

Synopsys completed its acquisition of simulation software maker Ansys in a cash-and-stock deal valued at roughly 35 billion dollars at announcement. The combination joins EDA chip-design tools with system-level simulation as silicon design converges with physical and AI system design.

The Department of Energy closed a 2.26 billion dollar loan to Lithium Americas to fund construction of Phase 1 of the Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada. It ranks among the largest US government financings of a mining project on record and set the template for federal balance-sheet support of domestic lithium supply.

Apple announced a 500 million dollar commitment to purchase US-made rare earth magnets from MP Materials' Fort Worth plant and to develop a recycling line at Mountain Pass. The deal added a marquee commercial anchor customer to a magnet supply chain previously underwritten mainly by the Pentagon.

The Department of Energy's Loan Programs Office announced a conditional commitment of roughly 755 million dollars in loans to Novonix to build synthetic graphite anode capacity in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Graphite became a policy priority after Chinese export licensing, making the commitment a direct midstream de-risking move.

The US Army awarded AeroVironment a contract with a ceiling of approximately 990 million dollars for Switchblade loitering munitions under its directed-requirement program. The award moved loitering munitions from urgent-need buys toward programmatic procurement at scale.

Anduril announced Arsenal-1, a roughly 900 million dollar hyperscale manufacturing plant near Columbus, Ohio, to mass-produce autonomous systems and weapons. The plant is the clearest test of whether attritable systems can be built at commercial rates rather than aerospace rates.

Counter-drone specialist Epirus raised a 250 million dollar Series D to scale production of its Leonidas high-power microwave system. The raise underlines how counter-UAS is drawing growth capital as drone threats proliferate faster than fielded defences.

L3Harris expanded solid rocket motor production capacity at its Camden, Arkansas campus, supported by Defense Production Act investment awarded to Aerojet Rocketdyne. The expansion targets higher motor output for GMLRS, Javelin and other munitions programs running at replenishment rates.

The US Department of Defense agreed to purchase 400 million dollars of MP Materials preferred stock, set a price floor of 110 dollars per kilogram for NdPr, and committed to offtake from a planned 10X magnet facility. The deal effectively underwrites ex-China NdFeB magnet supply for defence systems and the motors robotics depends on.

Figure AI closed a Series C round of over 1 billion dollars at a roughly 39 billion dollar post-money valuation, led by Parkway Venture Capital with participation including NVIDIA and Intel Capital. Proceeds fund humanoid manufacturing scale-up and continued development of its Helix embodied AI model.

Symbotic agreed to acquire Walmart's Advanced Systems and Robotics business for 200 million dollars upfront plus up to 350 million dollars in earnouts, while Walmart committed roughly 520 million dollars toward developing automated pickup and delivery centres. The deal deepens the largest disclosed customer relationship in warehouse robotics.

Google signed a definitive agreement to acquire cloud security company Wiz for roughly 32 billion dollars in cash, the largest cybersecurity acquisition on record. The deal folds cloud-native security into Google Cloud and marks hyperscalers as direct consolidators of the security market.

Palo Alto Networks announced a definitive agreement to acquire identity security leader CyberArk for roughly 25 billion dollars in cash and stock. The deal extends platformisation into identity and privileged access, framed by management around securing the coming wave of AI-agent identities.

Cisco completed its roughly 28 billion dollar all-cash acquisition of Splunk, the largest deal in its history. The combination pairs Cisco's network telemetry with Splunk's SIEM and observability data platform, consolidating the security-operations tier under a networking incumbent.

Rubrik priced its NYSE initial public offering at 32 dollars per share, raising roughly 752 million dollars. The listing validated cyber resilience and data security as a standalone public-market category and reopened the IPO window for security vendors.

PsiQuantum closed a 1 billion USD Series E led by BlackRock-managed funds at a valuation of about 7 billion USD, with participation including NVIDIA's venture arm. Proceeds fund its photonic fault-tolerant quantum computer sites in Brisbane and Chicago.

Honeywell-majority-owned Quantinuum closed an approximately 600 million USD equity round at a 10 billion USD pre-money valuation, with investors including NVIDIA's venture arm. The round doubled the 5 billion USD valuation set in its January 2024 raise.

IonQ agreed to acquire UK trapped-ion chip developer Oxford Ionics for approximately 1.075 billion USD, paid almost entirely in stock. The deal consolidates trapped-ion talent and IP and extends IonQ's acquisition streak across quantum networking and hardware.

The Australian federal and Queensland governments committed roughly 940 million AUD (about 620 million USD) in equity, grants and loans to PsiQuantum to build a fault-tolerant photonic quantum computer near Brisbane. It remains one of the largest single government commitments to a quantum company on record.

In January 2024 NASA increased the funded value of its Commercial LEO Destinations Space Act Agreement supporting Voyager's Starlab commercial space station by 57.5 million dollars, bringing the total award to 217.5 million dollars. The additional milestone funding supports design maturation and risk-reduction work intended to keep a commercial destination on track ahead of ISS retirement.

actor: US Navy Office of Naval Research
summary: In July 2022 the Office of Naval Research, part of the US Navy, awarded Frequency Electronics a contract worth approximately 20.3 million dollars to develop a mercury ion atomic clock based on technology from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Caltech. The award covers a 24-month base period with two option periods and funds pre-production prototypes of a next-generation precision timing standard for government applications.

American Superconductor received Ship Protection System orders valued at over 75 million dollars covering its advanced degaussing systems for the US Navy's San Antonio-class amphibious ships, placed through the lead shipbuilder. It ranked among the largest military orders in the company's history and anchors the defence side of its power systems business alongside its grid voltage-control hardware.

The US Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration awarded enCore Energy a contract to sell 100,000 pounds of US-origin uranium concentrate at $70.50 per pound into the national Uranium Reserve, worth about $7 million. enCore was one of five qualified US producers selected in the government's first domestic uranium purchase in roughly 40 years, and it simultaneously applied to join the DOE HALEU Consortium.

actor: US Department of Energy (Idaho National Laboratory)
summary: Lightbridge signed a seven-year umbrella Cooperative Research and Development Agreement and a Strategic Partnership Project agreement with Battelle Energy Alliance, the US Department of Energy contractor that operates Idaho National Laboratory, to develop and test its metallic Lightbridge Fuel. The framework built on earlier DOE GAIN voucher awards that funded fuel sample work and irradiation experiment design at INL for the company's fuel qualification path.

Nvidia selected Navitas Semiconductor to collaborate on its next-generation 800 V HVDC data-center power architecture supporting Kyber rack-scale systems that power Rubin Ultra GPUs. The collaboration, announced on 21 May 2025, applies Navitas GaNFast gallium-nitride and GeneSiC silicon-carbide power devices to Nvidia's rack-level power delivery chain; no investment amount was disclosed.

The US Department of Energy Loan Programs Office announced a conditional commitment for a loan of up to 754.8 million dollars (692 million dollars of principal plus 62.8 million dollars of capitalized interest) to Novonix to finance a new synthetic graphite manufacturing plant in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The commitment remains conditional on environmental review and technical, legal and financial requirements before definitive financing documents are executed.
sourceName: US Department of Energy Loan Programs Office

summary: Lithium Americas closed a 2.26 billion dollar loan from the US Department of Energy under the Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing program on October 28, 2024 to finance construction of Phase 1 processing facilities at Thacker Pass in Nevada. The loan comprises 1.97 billion dollars of principal plus roughly 290 million dollars of capitalized interest and supports a targeted 40,000 tonnes per year of battery-quality lithium carbonate.
sourceName: US Department of Energy / Lithium Americas news release

summary: The US Department of Defense awarded Perpetua Resources a Technology Investment Agreement of up to 24.8 million dollars under Title III of the Defense Production Act in December 2022 to advance permitting and engineering for the Stibnite gold-antimony project in Idaho. The agreement was later modified in early 2024 with an additional 34.4 million dollars, bringing total DPA funding to 59.2 million dollars for the only meaningful domestic US antimony resource.
sourceName: US Department of Defense / Perpetua Resources press release

summary: The Wyoming Energy Authority, with authorization from the Wyoming governor, awarded Ramaco Resources a 6.1 million dollar matching grant to help fund construction of a rare earth and critical minerals pilot processing facility at the Brook Mine near Sheridan, Wyoming. The grant supports development of what would be the first new US rare earth mine since the 1950s, targeting rare earth elements hosted in coal seams that federal researchers have characterized as one of the largest unconventional deposits of its kind.

The US Army 101st Airborne Division placed an order with Unusual Machines for 3,500 NDAA-compliant drone motors, built at the company's new Orlando, Florida facility, to support the division's Attritable Battlefield Enabler (A.B.E.) V1.01 drones. The order also covers US-made Blue UAS-listed components including the Aura analog camera, Aura VTX, Brave flight controller, and Brave ESC, and the Army indicated plans to expand procurement toward an additional roughly 20,000 components from the company in 2026.

actor: US Department of Defense (Defense Innovation Unit)
summary: The US Department of Defense's Defense Innovation Unit awarded Amprius Technologies a 10.5 million dollar contract in July 2025 to expand its Fremont, California pilot line toward 10 MWh of NDAA-compliant silicon-anode cell capacity, covering more than half of the build-out cost. A follow-on 1.5 million dollar addition in August 2025 brought the total to roughly 12 million dollars, anchoring domestic supply of the high energy density cells used in drones and other autonomous systems.
sourceName: Amprius Technologies investor letter / Manufacturing Dive

summary: On 15 August 2023 the US Transportation Security Administration announced that Telos Corporation had become its second official TSA PreCheck enrollment provider, with enrollment beginning at 10 initial locations. Telos has since expanded this government-backed identity enrollment network past 500 locations nationwide, including retail sites inside Office Depot and OfficeMax stores.

NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center awarded Quantum Computing Inc a prime contract to test its Dirac-3 photonic optimization machine on phase unwrapping of interferometric synthetic aperture radar imagery used in remote-sensing research. The contract value was not disclosed and is understood to be small, but it is one of the company's few named US government engagements.

actor: US Department of Commerce (CHIPS Program Office)
summary: The US Department of Commerce finalized an award of approximately 16 million USD in direct funding to SkyWater Technology under the CHIPS and Science Act to modernize and expand its Bloomington, Minnesota fab. The DoD Trusted Foundry accredited facility produces specialty and defense-related microelectronics and fabricates superconducting chips for quantum developers including D-Wave.

Microsoft signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement with Helion Energy: 50 MW or greater from Helion's first plant targeted for 2028, with financial penalties for non-delivery. Constellation acts as power marketer.

DOE announced the 8 selectees of the Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program with $46M obligated for the first 18 months: Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Focused Energy, Princeton Stellarators, Realta Fusion, Tokamak Energy Inc, Type One Energy, Xcimer Energy and Zap Energy. Cost-shared, NASA-COTS-style pilot-plant design program; awardees have since raised over $350M in follow-on private capital.
sourceName: U.S. Department of Energy announcement / ANS Nuclear Newswire

summary: Nucor and Helion agreed to develop a 500 MW fusion power plant at a Nucor steelmaking facility targeting 2030 operations, with Nucor making a direct $35M investment in Helion - the first industrial-scale fusion offtake commitment outside tech.

actor: Lightspeed Venture Partners, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and a major university endowment (new investors), with Sam Altman, Nucor and other existing investors
summary: Helion Energy raised a $425M Series F at a $5.4B post-money valuation to scale its Polaris prototype and Orion plant toward the Microsoft PPA, taking total funding past $1B.

Google signed the largest direct corporate fusion offtake to date: 200 MW, half the output of Commonwealth Fusion Systems' first 400 MW ARC plant in Chesterfield County, Virginia (grid power expected early 2030s), and increased its equity stake in CFS with options on future plants.
sourceName: CFS press release / PR Newswire / ANS Nuclear Newswire

actor: Nvidia (NVentures), Google, Breakthrough Energy Ventures and a Mitsubishi-led Japanese consortium
summary: Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised an oversubscribed $863M Series B2 - the largest energy or deep-tech round since 2021 - with Nvidia as a first-time investor, bringing total funding to nearly $3B to complete SPARC and progress the Virginia ARC plant.

Eni, a CFS shareholder since 2018, signed a power purchase agreement worth more than $1B for decarbonized power from the 400 MW ARC plant in Chesterfield County, Virginia - the second offtake on that plant in three months after Google.

At CES 2026, CFS unveiled a digital twin of the SPARC tokamak built with Nvidia Omniverse and Siemens industrial software, as SPARC reached roughly 75 percent completion with the first of 18 toroidal field magnets installed and first plasma targeted for 2027.

Furukawa Electric and Tokamak Energy announced a step-up in collaboration to explore developing UK high-temperature superconducting tape capability, starting with an initial programme of tape research, development, prototyping and feasibility assessment - extending their 2023 supply agreement (several hundred kilometres of HTS tape for ST80-HTS) and Furukawa's December 2023 GBP 10M investment in Tokamak Energy. In April 2026 Furukawa was also named Magnet Systems Partner for the UK Government STEP fusion programme under a GBP 70M contract running to 2029, with the STEP prototype expected to use an estimated 30,000 km of HTS tape; the June 2026 agreement was signed at 10 Downing Street under the UK-Japan Frontier Technology Partnership.
sourceName: Furukawa Electric press release (2026-06-15) / World Nuclear News

actor: Fusion for Energy (European Union domestic agency for ITER)
summary: Air Liquide was awarded a further EUR 65M ITER contract by Fusion for Energy (two nitrogen refrigerators and 80K helium loop boxes) on top of its 2012 EUR 83M liquid-helium plant contract with the ITER Organization, making it builder of the world's largest fusion cryoplant; a third contract (19 cryolines for ITER-India) followed in October 2015, and commissioning runs through mid-2026 per Fusion for Energy. Anchors the cryogenics node.
sourceName: Air Liquide press release (2014-05-22) / iter.org / Fusion for Energy
